The user wants me to decide eligibility for four benefits for a household based on the given facts and rule clauses. I need to output JSON with decisions for each benefit.

He is liable for council tax, annual net £1,205.19. He needs care help (yes), for 24 months, day and night. Electricity bill in name.

Assessment date: 2026-10-27.

Now evaluate each benefit.

1. Pension Credit (Guarantee Credit)
Rules: PC-1: Claimant must live in England, Scotland, or Wales and have reached State Pension age. F3: country=England, F24: age 67, F25: state pension age 66. So meets.
PC-2: Claimant must include partner; both partners must have reached State Pension age. F4: has_partner=no. So no partner condition needed.
PC-3: Savings up to £10,000 ignored; above that, every £500 or part thereof counts as £1 weekly income. Savings £2,752 < £10,000, so ignored.
PC-4: Guarantee Credit tops up weekly income to £238 (single) or £363.25 (couple); eligible if assessed income below threshold. Single threshold £238. Assessed weekly income = weekly income total + savings income (none). Weekly income total = £184.32 (F6, F13). That's below £238. So eligible.
PC-5: Weekly Guarantee Credit amount is the difference between threshold and assessed weekly income. So amount = £238 - £184.32 = £53.68 per week.

But need to check if any other income? Only weekly_income_total given. Savings ignored. So eligible.

Decision: eligible, weekly_amount = 53.68.

Clause IDs: PC-1, PC-2, PC-3, PC-4, PC-5. Fact IDs: F1, F2, F3, F4, F6, F11, F13, F24, F25.

2. Attendance Allowance
Rules: AA-1: Must have reached State Pension age. Yes, age 67 > 66.
AA-2: Must have a physical or mental disability or health condition severe enough to need help with personal care or supervision. F19: needs_care_help = yes.
AA-3: Must have needed that help for at least 6 months. F20: care_need_months = 24 > 6.
AA-4: Must have been in Great Britain for at least 2 of the last 3 years. F5: in_gb_2_of_last_3_years = yes.
AA-5: Cannot get Attendance Allowance if already receiving DLA, PIP, or Adult Disability Payment. F9: receives_dla_or_pip = no.
AA-6: Paid at £76.70/week (lower rate) or £114.60/week (higher rate); higher rate when help needed both day and night. F21: care_day_and_night = yes. So higher rate applies.
AA-7: Scheme covers England and Wales; people in Scotland apply for Pension Age Disability Payment. F3: country=England, so covered.

All conditions met. Eligible for higher rate £114.60/week.

Rules: CTR-1: Available to people on low income or claiming benefits, up to 100% reduction. Pensioners in England and Wales.
CTR-2: Applies to people who have reached State Pension age. Yes.
CTR-3: Applicant must be liable to pay council tax on the home they live in. F16: council_tax_liable = yes.
CTR-4: People who get Guarantee Credit of Pension Credit get maximum reduction (100%). But F7: receives_pension_credit = no. However, we just determined he is eligible for Pension Credit Guarantee Credit. But the rule says "People who get the Guarantee Credit of Pension Credit get the maximum reduction". Does "get" mean currently receiving, or eligible? The fact says receives_pension_credit = no. But he might be eligible but not yet claiming. The rule likely means if they are in receipt. However, CTR-6 says "Otherwise, people with capital above £16,000 cannot get a reduction. Otherwise, the weekly reduction is the weekly net council tax charge... less 20% of any weekly income above the applicable amount. The applicable amount is the Pension Credit guarantee amount (£238 single, £363.25 couple). Income from savings follows Pension Credit rule... The household is eligible if the weekly reduction is greater than zero."

So we need to compute weekly reduction. Since he doesn't currently get Guarantee Credit (F7), we use CTR-6.

Capital: savings £2,752 < £16,000, so not excluded.

Weekly net council tax charge = annual net / 52 = £1,205.19 / 52 = £23.17673... approx £23.18.

Applicable amount = £238 (single).

Weekly income = £184.32. Income from savings: savings £2,752, first £10,000 ignored, so no savings income.

Income above applicable amount = £184.32 - £238 = negative, so zero.

Thus weekly reduction = weekly net council tax charge - 20% of (income above applicable) = £23.18 - 0 = £23.18 > 0. So eligible.

But wait: The rule says "less 20% of any weekly income above the applicable amount." Since income is below applicable amount, reduction is full weekly net council tax charge. So eligible for 100% reduction? Actually CTR-4 says if get Guarantee Credit, get 100% reduction. But CTR-6 says reduction is weekly net council tax charge less 20% of income above applicable. If income below applicable, reduction = weekly net council tax charge, which is 100% of net council tax. So effectively same.

Thus eligible. Weekly amount? The benefit is a reduction in council tax, not a weekly cash payment. The rule says "weekly reduction is the weekly net council tax charge...".
